label: early original-phase r/o/s/t input after r/f/z/3/o/p/l/c/k
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase: never at t=0, the delimiter, or the copy phase (1 activation out of 12.7k). Concentrated at positions 1-4 (t=1-3 hold ~87% of mass) and fades by t=6. Token-selective on the current input: r (9% rate, 35% of mass), then o, s, t, then 3, x, p, z, f; essentially silent on other tokens such as i, l, 2. Mostly the first occurrence of the token (90% of mass). Earlier context matters: rates are higher when the previous input is r, f, z, 3, o, p, l, c or k, and the strongest activations come on repeated r (e.g. k r r, y h r r). Even so, the right token at an early position fires only a minority of the time (r at t=1-3 has about 30% precision), so the remaining dependence on history is not captured. The predicate (r/o/s/t at t=1-4 after one of those previous tokens) gets dev F1 0.43, mass recall 0.57. Dropping the previous-token condition (any of the 9 tokens at t=1-4) catches 97% of mass but has only 11% precision.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=1: r, o, s, t; t=2: r, o, s, t; t=3: r, o, t, s) and the previous input (most: r, z, f, 3, o, l; least: 0, u, m, q); timing cues that raise it most: t=3, L=9 & t=10, t=2.
